[b]Ministry of Foreign Affairs[/b]

[i]بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم [/i]

We are deeply concerned about the conflicts currently taking place in [nation]Astanir[/nation] and [nation]Tallisland[/nation]. We do not take sides in these conflicts, but instead would urge all parties to exercise restraint and refrain from actions that could endanger civilians, damage or destroy civilian infrastructure, or otherwise harm the safety and livelihood of the civilians in these areas. 

Furthermore, and above all, we strongly encourage peace talks between all factions (including those nations who are supporting various factions in these conflicts), either directly or through mediation involving the IA, EEHP, and EDU. We thank the government of [nation]BR Bob[/nation] for taking the first step, in shaa Allah, towards a just and lasting peace in both the aforementioned countries.

We also strongly rebuke external involvement in the internal affairs of these countries, as this can deepen the conflict and lead to unexpected consequences in these countries, regions, and the world at large. Quite often, when large amounts of weapons and munitions are sent into active war zones, they end up proliferating beyond these zones and contribute to further conflicts and violence even after wars end.

Finally, we would like to encourage an urgent IA and/or EEHP meeting regarding these wars, how they could be ended, and what could be done to protect civilians on all sides. In shaa Allah, there will be peace and inclusive governance for all people in both these countries.

[i]Abdoul Mahonomayi
Foreign Minister of the Islamic Sultanate of Baladullah[/i]
[/spoiler]

Admiral Fredrik Madsen stood on the bridge of the Niels Juel, a Niels class frigate in the 1st Carrier Strike Group. He was a grizzled sailor who had served as the head of the strike group since the Sal-Baliz incursions, he commanded the loyalty of the officers and seamen of the strike group and was a key figure in the royal court, especially with the ladies of the court.

Now as he had embarked on his second tour as an Admiral, he considered the dangers that lay ahead, apparently the Neue Republik had laid propulsion disablers and had enacted a heavy blockade of the strait with its navy. Madsen didnt want any confrontation with the Neue Republik as much as the government of Thýven, however, he had ordered the strike group to be prepared.

[spoiler=sorry it took so long lol]
The first sparks of the governments collapse were now crackling in pinewood. Two naval marine vessels joined a takeover of the Maarja Isles via a coup of the government within the capital city of Eluoja. The rebels at Ivon were kicking the Gythenan army out of the city with a quite impressive haste. There was no denying it now, the old republic would not be able to handle the weight of revolution.

And in the city of Polijamsa, things were finally boiling over. A group of young men had begun to rally against the government in the streets. As the day went on, word spread like leaves on a fall day about the matter, and numerous people were joining in the protests now. As a mob began swelling in size, movement was made towards the building housing the citys government, and, unbeknownst to them, the diplomatic envoys from Sanguivallis.

As the Sanguinians began collecting info on the current revolutionary movement, Mr. Niskala, who now was feeling a sense of false calm, continued on with his conversation. Perhaps he could convince the Sanguinians to, maybe, look past ideological differences and help a fellow nation in need. Or, simply, do not bother with the civil conflict and continue with things as normal. He was very wrong.

As Mr. Niskala continued on, discussing foreign affairs and trade, the crowd loomed closer in, up the streets and around the blocs. The crowd carried weapons, some owned with them a rifle, others simply brought rakes and axes.

Within the parliament building, things were tense but calm. Well, I do believe I could interest you in, perhaps, pinewood from Laskiiland, up north? They have amazing views up th-

The looming presence of a mob finally makes its presence known. Mr. Niskala and the Sanguinians both heard noises from outside, however they were indistinguishable for a few minutes. By the time they could tell what it was, it was far too late. The mob had arrived, and they were breaking through the locked door.

[i][b]The Opening Arrival of the USO Navy Fleet[/b]

The 1st Carrier Strike Group arrived in the Straits on July 15. Admiral Lenor Advert got word that Thýven was setting up a blockade to prevent the USO from intervening in the conflict. Lenor Advert, commanding from the carrier OAS Freedom, knew that any misstep could trigger a war with Thývens blockade forces. His first order was to establish a defensive perimeter around the task group, ensuring all ships maintained anti-submarine and radar surveillance at maximum range.

The destroyers and frigates fanned out into a wide screening formation while the carrier remained centered as the command node. Electronic warfare suites were activated to detect and jam any hostile transmissions from the Neue Republik or Thýven vessels.

Lenor Advert instructed reconnaissance drones and maritime patrol aircraft to map out the blockades composition, distance, and vulnerability gaps. The Amphibious Squadron, carrying blue water fleets of the Marine Expeditionary Force, was ordered to remain 40 miles south, ready to deploy if the situation escalated.

Lenor Advert orders to avoid direct engagement but ensure that the USO fleet begins subtle maneuvering drills, testing Thývens reaction time while gathering intelligence on their command patterns. By nightfall, Advert had positioned the fleet in a strategic holding arc, allowing rapid response to any provocation a message that the USO Navy was prepared to defend its interests without firing the first shot.

Lenor Advert Got any word from Thýven? 

A communications officer turned from his console. Negative, Admiral. No direct transmission. However... he hesitated, glancing at his monitor, their fleet has been increased speed. Three destroyers and a cruiser are holding position at the peak of the exclusion zone.

Advert  So theyre watching us.

Yes, sir. Passive radar pings every thirty seconds. Theyre tracking our formation.

The admiral folded his hands behind his back, his gaze steady. Maintain course and formation. If they want a stare down, theyll get one. But we wont be the first to blink. These deer people can't understand true human nature? Aye, bring me those two furry. You know Valks and Urek? Those deer boy, they can help us to translate with their specie. They might help us establish contact and avoid a misunderstanding.

"Um, sir? You know they are both different, the deer people are from Elseyr while ours are from Argos."
